step_goal: Turn deck identity, card metadata, and online research into the machine-readable semantic contract that every compiler consumes before emitting Mulligan, GlobalValues, CardID, Combo, Presume, or Concede artifacts.
reliable_uses: Define the pre-config semantic control plane that HSConfig should build after deck intake and deck research, but before any VisionAI file emission.

Specify a gameplan contract that records archetype, speed, win condition, mulligan anchors, matchup posture, target policy, trade posture, resource policy, hero power policy, combo sequencing, and known bad patterns as static Step 1 semantics rather than runtime claims.

Use `gameplan_contract.json` as the stable source of truth for `correct_play_semantics`, so later compilers can lower only explicit rules into `Mulligan.json`, per-card `CARDID.json`, `Combo.json`, or `GlobalValues.json`.

Require every decoded deck card to receive explicit static coverage through `per_card_roles`, `correct_play_semantics.card_usage`, `card_gameplan_coverage_report.json`, and `card_obligation_matrix.json` instead of allowing silent fallback gaps.

Keep archetype-wide guidance and exact-list card guidance separate, so HSConfig can inherit a general archetype posture while still attaching per-card obligations only to cards that exist in the submitted deck.

Preserve uncertainty and unsupported advice in contract-visible structures such as `unknowns`, low-confidence posture rows, or suppression reports instead of translating symbolic guidance directly into runtime JSON.

Define Step 2 detector anchors up front by making `correct_play_semantics` keys stable across mulligan, card usage, targeting, hero power, resource use, generated entities, lethal setup, and mechanic-specific policy families.

Keep the Step 1 boundary strict: the contract may describe intended play and expected config surfaces, but it does not prove config load, actual runtime decisions, gameplay improvement, or patch correctness.
limitations: Static gameplan construction cannot prove `CONFIG_LOAD_OK`, `RUNTIME_SAMPLED`, `PLAN_CONFIRMED`, `FINETUNE_READY`, or gameplay improvement; those remain fresh post-run evidence claims only.

Archetype labels, matchup posture, mulligan anchors, and face-versus-trade heuristics are meta-sensitive and must remain source-cited, date-stamped, and confidence-scored rather than treated as timeless facts.
Deckstring decode and card metadata can identify exact cards, but they cannot by themselves prove target timing, combo windows, hero power transformation behavior, or correct resource sequencing.
Official VisionAI pages define syntax and documented semantics, but they do not decide when a symbolic gameplan statement is safe to compile into a live runtime row.

Some desirable plan concepts, such as flexible matchup branches, generated-card contingencies, hidden-information lines, or soft trade heuristics, may need to stay as contract clauses or suppression diagnostics instead of becoming emitted config rules.
Per-card coverage is only trustworthy when every deck card is represented either by an explicit contract row or by an explicit contract-gap row; silent omissions make downstream audits unreliable.

GlobalValues is a deck-wide, high-risk surface; the gameplan contract may describe board-value intent, but it must not authorize speculative deck-wide tuning without the copied runtime baseline and later fresh evidence.
Documented but unsupported surfaces such as `Concede.json` and `Presume.json` should stay outside the default Step 05 compile path even if the broader research stack records them.
aggressive_generation_policy: Every decoded card must receive an explicit role, usage expectation, or contract_gap; no card may disappear into generic fallback.
Use guide-backed archetype posture to define face/trade, resource, target, mulligan, and combo expectations before config compilation.
Prefer explicit low-confidence semantics over omission, because later compilers can still turn low-confidence claims into report-only rows or cautious preview intent.
Do not wait for gameplay logs; this skill assumes static guide-aligned generation and uses evidence quality only to shape confidence and output surface.
validation_gates: Every deck card must be present in card_role_map and card_usage_expectations or in a named contract_gap.
Every gameplan clause must cite source_evidence_index or card_metadata_snapshot provenance.
Every intended runtime surface must be represented in config_surface_intent_map before compiler execution.
Unknowns must be explicit and machine-readable.
The contract must not claim CONFIG_LOAD_OK, runtime proof, winrate proof, or post-run tuning correctness.
architectural_implications: Step 05 should build `gameplan_contract.json` before any config compiler runs, and every later emitted runtime row should point back to a stable gameplan clause or explicit suppression reason.

The contract should mirror the implemented schema shape: deck identity, archetype summary, matchup assumptions, win condition, mulligan plan, curve policy, pressure turns, per-card roles, target policy, trade policy, reach policy, resource policy, hero power policy, choice policy, generated-entities policy, combo sequencing, board-value contract, unknowns, research pack, and source refs.

Archetype and speed belong in the semantic layer, not in filename conventions or free-text notes; the contract should expose them as machine-readable descriptors that downstream coverage, detectors, and preview compilers can read deterministically.

Mulligan anchors should be stored in a source-backed plan with `default_keep`, `conditional_keep`, `default_throw`, rationale, and source refs, while matchup- or coin-specific logic stays explicit and suppressible if the runtime-safe compiler cannot express it.

Per-card coverage should be mandatory: every deck card should have role tags, usage expectations, target-owner posture when applicable, hold policy, forbidden actions, parser requirements, confidence markers, and stable `gameplan_clause_refs` for Step 2 linkage.

Face-versus-trade posture should not be a vague deck summary. It should be represented as explicit `target_policy`, `trade_policy`, `reach_policy`, and card-level or matchup-level exceptions so detectors can judge visible contradictions later.

Resource policy and hero power policy should remain separate global semantics and also flow into per-card obligations where needed, because later audits need both deck-wide rules and card-specific exceptions.

Combo sequencing should require concrete ordered chains, role labels such as setup or payoff, same-turn versus cross-turn separation, and emission eligibility; symbolic synergy notes alone should not authorize `Combo.json` output.

Known bad patterns should remain machine-readable and scoped to a card, role tag, matchup tag, detector family, or global policy so they become auditable anti-patterns instead of accidental runtime patch hints.

The contract should feed Step 2 directly by keeping `correct_play_semantics` keys stable, generating `decision_trace_requirements.json`, and building `card_obligation_matrix.json` from the same clause set rather than from separate informal notes.

GlobalValues intent should be modeled as board-value policy and allowed overlay posture inside the contract, but the default emission path should still copy the real runtime baseline first and limit overlays to explicitly authorized keys only.

The Step 05 build should fail closed when archetype posture is stale, card coverage is incomplete, a key policy family is missing, or a requested runtime surface depends on unsupported or undocumented semantics.
recommended_contracts: `gameplan_contract.json`: the main semantic source of truth that captures archetype, speed, win condition, mulligan plan, card roles, card usage expectations, target and trade posture, resource policy, hero power policy, combo sequencing, board-value intent, unknowns, and source refs.

`deck_research_contract.json`: the upstream per-card evidence bundle that provides role tags, usage expectations, forbidden actions, parser requirements, confidence levels, contract gaps, and source-backed card-level semantics before Step 05 composes the higher-level gameplan.

`archetype_research.json`: an upstream archetype document with primary win conditions, mulligan anchors, resource posture, board posture, face-versus-trade rules, combo or synergy dependencies, unsupported mechanics, and known bad patterns.

`mulligan_anchor_map.json`: a research-stage artifact that stores default keeps, conditional keeps, matchup-conditioned keeps, coin or no-coin branches, and rationale before safe down-compilation into runtime mulligan rows.

`matchup_posture_assumptions.json`: a contract that keeps default posture plus opponent-archetype-conditioned posture rows separate from unconditional deck rules, with confidence and freshness markers.

`known_bad_patterns.json`: a machine-readable anti-pattern registry that scopes each known failure mode to cards, role tags, matchup tags, or global policies so Step 2 detectors and review tools can cite them consistently.

`card_gameplan_coverage_report.json`: a mandatory completeness diagnostic that proves every deck card is covered by a stable semantic row or an explicit visible gap before config preview generation starts.

`card_obligation_matrix.json`: the Step 2-facing per-card obligation surface that derives from the gameplan and preserves card usage, target posture, resource policy, and known bad patterns as observation contracts only.

`decision_trace_requirements.json`: the machine-readable evidence contract that tells Step 2 which parser fields, option surfaces, target data, and result-state links are needed to judge each gameplan clause.

`config_surface_intent_map.json`: a routing artifact that maps each accepted gameplan claim to `Mulligan.json`, per-card `CARDID.json`, `Combo.json`, `GlobalValues.json`, or report-only suppression so the compiler path stays explicit.
never_autogenerate_without: Exact deck identity inputs, including deck name, deck code, resolved card list, card IDs, and stable deck fingerprint data from `deck_intake.json`.
A validated `deck_research_contract.json` with explicit per-card coverage or explicit contract-gap rows for every deck card; Step 05 should not invent missing card semantics silently.

A validated `gameplan_contract.json` that includes mulligan semantics, per-card usage expectations, target posture, trade posture, resource policy, hero power policy, combo sequencing, board-value intent, unknowns, and source refs before any config preview compilation begins.
Source-backed archetype and matchup inputs with freshness, confidence, and citations recorded for every high-level strategic claim used by the gameplan builder.

Stable `correct_play_semantics` coverage for all detector-relevant families that the target deck actually needs, including at minimum mulligan, card usage, target policy, hero power policy, resource policy, choice policy, generated entities policy, combo sequencing, and any required mechanic-specific families.
A human-visible coverage diagnostic, such as `card_gameplan_coverage_report.json`, proving that no deck card fell out of the semantic layer unnoticed.
Suppression or gap reporting for any symbolic, unsupported, stale, or runtime-unsafe advice that cannot be lowered cleanly into documented VisionAI syntax.

Runtime-surface validation boundaries that keep `Concede.json`, `Presume.json`, undocumented conditions, and hidden-information assumptions out of the default Step 05 emission path unless first-class support is added.
The real runtime `GlobalValues.json` baseline and key-profile knowledge before any deck-wide global-values generation or overlay authorization is allowed.
A strict Step 1 authority boundary: pre-run contracts may authorize preview generation and guarded apply readiness only, never runtime-proof claims or autonomous gameplay-tuning claims.
